newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Merck details migraine drug test results.
newsitem.headline: Merck details migraine drug test results.

text.p: Merck and Co said on Wednesday a study had shown that its new oral migraine drug MAXALT (rizatriptan benzoate) provided significantly faster and more complete pain relief than the market leader, sumatriptan.

Merck said the international trial also showed that 10 mg of MAXALT, which is under development, helped more patients become pain free within two hours than 100 mg of sumatriptan, the Glaxo-Wellcome drug marketed as Imigran/Imitrex.
The results of the study involving 1,099 patients were presented for the first time at the 8th Congress of the International Headache Society in Amsterdam.

Merck said the trial showed that MAXALT showed statistically significant improvements over sumatriptan in the number of patients who experienced headache relief at one hour, became pain free at 1.5 to two hours, had no nausea at 0.5 to two hours and were able to function normally at one to two hours.
Sumatriptan is estimated to have more than 70 percent of the worldwide market for prescription migraine medicines, worth at least $1.1 billion a year.
A number of other drugs to relieve the acute pain of migraine headaches are under development, including Zeneca Group's zolmitriptan, marketed as Zomig.
